name: Connecticut

flag.description: A blue field with a white rococo shield showing three grapevines, above a white streamer reading QUI TRANSTULIT SUSTINET.
flag.symbolism: The three grapevines are often said to represent the colony's first three towns, Windsor, Wethersfield and Hartford, transplanted from England.

hook: Connecticut's seal-on-blue is the one with just three grapevines on a white shield, with no people or animals at all.
trivia: The Latin motto means "He who transplanted still sustains".
The colonial seal once showed fifteen grapevines; the number was cut to three in 1711.
